name: Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior
description: Detection, monitoring and theorization of coordinated link-sharing and coordinated inauthentic networks on social media platforms, including the CooRnet/CLSB methodology, the VERA-AI Alert system, and studies of deceptive information operations (e.g. 'Zombie Internet', gambling promotion networks). This is the researcher's longest-running and most active methodological signature line.

name: Information Disorder & Disinformation
description: Broad conceptual and empirical work on fake news, misinformation and disinformation circulation within hybrid media systems, including the PROMPT project monitoring EU disinformation narratives and foundational taxonomy-building on misleading information.

name: Platform Governance & Research Data Access
description: Research and policy engagement on social media platform accountability, API/data-access regimes (CrowdTangle shutdown, Meta's URL Shares Dataset, DSA-era research APIs), and critical assessment of Meta's content moderation and political content reduction policies, including the researcher's JRC/ECAT expert work under DSA Article 40(12).

name: Political Polarization & Partisanship
description: Analysis of partisan news ecosystems, affective and insular community dynamics, algorithmic amplification of extremes, and partisan attention metrics on social media, spanning Italian, Brazilian and cross-national contexts.

name: Generative AI & LLMs in Communication Research
description: Methodological work on integrating large language models and generative AI into content analysis and classification pipelines for social media research, plus study of generative AI's use in deceptive persuasion campaigns and peer review.

name: Italian Electoral Communication
description: The MINE programme's core empirical focus: mapping Italian news media and social media dynamics around national elections (2018, 2022), political parallelism, hyperpartisan networks, and campaign-specific case studies (e.g. the 'Seaside Campaign').

name: Health Misinformation & Fact-Checking
description: Studies of problematic health information circulation on social media, including COVID-19 fact-checking acceleration tools and coordinated networks spreading health misinformation in India and Nigeria.

name: Cross-National Disinformation Networks
description: Comparative mapping of coordinated information campaigns and political advertising across countries beyond Italy, including Germany's 2021 federal election, Brazil's post-Bolsonaro digital battlefield, Nigeria, India, and Latin America more broadly.

name: Social Media Engagement & Audience Metrics
description: Research on how users interact with and are affected by platform features—reactions, reach, algorithmic governance, and engagement patterns—particularly on Facebook, including systematic reviews and partisan audience dynamics.

name: Digital Methods & Computational Social Science
description: Foundational and pedagogical work on computational approaches to studying social and media systems—from sociocybernetics theory to social network analysis, survey recruitment via platform ads, and data-ethics—underpinning the researcher's teaching and tool development.

name: Platforms, Audiences, and Online Communities
description: Empirical and reflective studies of how platform affordances, cultures, and audience practices shape online sociality, identity, and community formation across sites like Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, Twitter/Mastodon, and LiveJournal.

name: Critical Analysis of AI Industry Imaginaries and Discourse
description: Studies examining how AI industry actors, media, and communities construct and circulate narratives, imaginaries, and framings (e.g., longtermism, techno-hagiography, 'quiet futuring', political-economy 'decoys') that shape public understanding and obscure or legitimize the underlying power structures of AI development.

name: Reflections on the State of Misinformation and Online Harm Research
description: Papers that step back from primary empirical study to critically assess the misinformation/online-harms research field itself — diagnosing biases (e.g., WEIRD-centrism, overreliance on cognitive proxies), mapping gaps in evidence (causal, longitudinal, cross-national), and proposing directions or borrowed lessons (e.g., from climate psychology) to make the field more rigorous and generalizable.

name: Theorizing AI's Social Role: Agency, Trust, and Public Perception
description: Papers that apply or extend social theory and communication-trust frameworks to understand the societal position of AI systems, ranging from conceptual demarcations of machine agency and formal multi-agent social frameworks to models of public trust in generative AI and empirical survey data on public attitudes toward AI adoption.

name: Computational Studies of Political Media and Advertising
description: Papers using large-scale computational or quasi-experimental methods to study political advertising, media capture, and ideological signaling on digital platforms, including causal analysis of ad effects, detection of covert advertiser influence on news coverage, and latent ideology estimation of political video content.

name: Survey Measurement Validity and Comparability
description: Papers examining methodological challenges in survey-based measurement, including whether respondents understand survey questions as intended, how online sample composition and quality checks affect representativeness and response validity, and how question wording and dataset differences affect cross-national and longitudinal comparability of trust measures.
